Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask. We're happy to accommodate a temporary Net45 pilot with a few standard guardrails so we can manage credit exposure while you ramp. Proposed terms (quick sketch):

- Pilot duration: 90 days (start of first invoice to end of pilot).
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices, Net45 for each invoice during the pilot window.
- Credit cap: $75,000 total exposure (sum of unpaid invoices).
- Initial requirement: Purchase Order (PO) and company VAT registration certificate for EU invoices.
- Optional deposit: 20% of the first estimated invoice amount to be paid before provisioning for larger pilots (> $50k MRR).
- Early-pay incentive: 2% discount if invoice paid within 10 days (applies to US invoices).
- VAT handling: we invoice net-of-VAT; for EU entities we need the VAT reg number to zero-rate (if reverse-charge applies) or include VAT if you prefer Redwood to collect — we'll follow the tax treatment you instruct but need the certificate to support zero-rating.

I've attached a short pilot-term-sheet that captures the above and a crude exposure calculator so your finance team can see what $75k credit cap looks like month-by-month. If you prefer a smaller credit cap or a deposit instead of a cap, we can adjust.

Next steps: if this looks directionally right I'll loop in Legal for a short amendment and Finance for final sign-off.

Thanks —

Aditya / Priyom — quick finance POV:

- Credit cap: recommend reducing to $50,000 for the pilot unless we receive a 20% advance on the first invoice. A $75k cap is ok for customers with solid payment history; Greenwave is new so lower cap is prudent.
- Deposit: if Greenwave can do a 20% deposit of the estimated first month we can keep the cap at $75k; otherwise cap to $50k.
- PO: require a PO for our records; invoices issued net-of-VAT where Greenwave provides VAT registration (if reverse-charge applies). If Greenwave prefers Redwood to collect VAT, we will but that introduces cashflow lag for them.
- Billing: recommend monthly invoices with Net45 but include an auto-escalation: if any invoice is 30+ days overdue we pause provisioning after 7 days' notice. Operationally we need this to limit token consumption risk.

If Laura wants to add contract language I can accept an internal approval to proceed with the $50k cap + 20% deposit option if Emily confirms.
